title: Test subprotocol runs the inside branch on reaching inputs
statement: Let $s$ be a subprotocol of a deterministic communication protocol $p$, and let $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ and $q_{\mathrm{out}}$ be two further protocols on the same input types. If the input pair $(x,y)$ reaches $s$ — that is, $x$ lies in Alice's reach set and $y$ in Bob's reach set for $s$ — then executing the test subprotocol built from $s$, $q_{\mathrm{in}}$, and $q_{\mathrm{out}}$ on $(x,y)$ yields the same output as executing $q_{\mathrm{in}}$ on $(x,y)$.
hypotheses_covered: s is a subprotocol of p (IsSubprotocol s p)
qIn and qOut are protocols on the same types
(x, y) reaches the subprotocol s (reaches hsp x y, i.e. x in reachX and y in reachY)
replaced:
If $(x, y)$ reaches the subprotocol $s$ of $p$, then
$(\texttt{testSubprotocol}\;\texttt{hsp}\;\texttt{qIn}\;\texttt{qOut}).\texttt{run}\;x\;y = \texttt{qIn}.\texttt{run}\;x\;y$.
